cards.headline: Open model matches frontier on maths benchmarks
cards.summary: A fictional lab released open weights for a model that scores within two points of closed systems on competition maths. It narrows the gap between open and closed models for reasoning tasks.

cards.headline: Regulators publish draft rules for AI audits
cards.summary: A made-up agency proposed yearly third-party audits for large models used in hiring and lending. Companies would have to publish test results and fix flagged bias within 90 days.

cards.headline: Chipmaker doubles inference capacity with new fab
cards.summary: A sample chip company said its new plant will double output of inference accelerators next year. Cheaper inference is what lets smaller teams ship AI features.

cards.headline: Hospitals trial AI notes with patient consent
cards.summary: Three fictional hospitals began a six-month trial of AI-drafted visit notes that patients can opt out of. Doctors review every note before it enters the record.

cards.headline: River treaty signed after decade of talks
cards.summary: Two invented countries agreed to share water from a border river, with a joint body setting seasonal quotas. The deal ends a dispute that had stalled farming on both banks.

cards.headline: Coastal city opens its first metro line
cards.summary: A sample city opened 14 km of driverless metro linking the port to the airport. Officials expect it to take 60,000 cars a day off the coast road.

cards.headline: Election turnout hits a twenty-year high
cards.summary: Turnout in a fictional national election reached 78 percent, driven by first-time voters. Results are due on Thursday after postal ballots are counted.

cards.headline: Wheat harvest beats forecasts despite dry spring
cards.summary: A made-up farm ministry reported a harvest 9 percent above forecast thanks to late rain. Bread prices, which rose sharply last year, are expected to ease.

cards.headline: The quiet craft of mapping the sea floor
cards.summary: An essay follows a survey ship charting a ridge nobody has seen. Most of the ocean floor is still mapped more coarsely than the surface of Mars.

cards.headline: Volunteers bring a lost orchard back to fruit
cards.summary: A village replanted 200 heritage apple trees from cuttings kept by one grower. The first harvest went to the school kitchen.
